newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Major moves closer to free vote on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Major moves closer to free vote on EMU.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major on Thursday appeared to strengthen a suggestion that if he won the May 1 election he would allow Conservative members of parliament a free vote on whether Britain should join a single European currency.

He told reporters it would be very difficult to imposse the traditional discipline of the whips', or parliamentary business managers', office on the party, which is deeply divided over whether Britain should join the single currency.
"In reality it would be very difficult to have a three-line whip anyway," Major said.

If Major did allow a free vote, he might garner some support from pro-European members of the opposition Labour and Liberal Democrat parties, but this would be at the cost of appearing to to be unable to control his own party.

Major said that the next European Union summit had been fixed for just 17 days after the British election because Britain's partners wanted to catch a new British prime minister "in the warm afterglow of the election".
Major, speaking to reporters on his campaign 'plane flying to Hawarden, northwest England, said: "It is no coincidence that they have called the EU summit 17 days after the election."
European leaders are planning an interim summit after the election to hear the views of Britain's new government ahead of a crucial June summit in Amsterdam.
The EU summit in Amsterdam will discuss the conclusion of the EU Inter-Governmental Conference reviewing the rules by which the bloc takes decisions.
Major said Blair was naive and inexperienced on EU matters and would be unable to deal with the complex questions involved.
"It's like playing multi-dimensional chess," Major said.
